verified.notes: Falcon Payload User's Guide 2025-05-09 PDF fetched (WebFetch returned binary; extracted locally with pypdf, 128pp). All three condensed fragments are verbatim on the page: (a) 'A single Merlin Vacuum (MVac) engine powers the second stage, using a fixed 165:1 expansion nozzle.' (165:1 number supported at the engine-nozzle basis); (b) 'Falcon launch vehicle avionics, and guidance, navigation, and control systems use a fault-tolerant architecture that provides full vehicle single-fault tolerance' (verbatim incl. 'full vehicle single-fault tolerance'); (c) '...restraint, release, and separation systems use pneumatic devices that provide low-shock release and positive force separation'. Excerpt's '...' elisions each correspond to a verbatim source sentence. Earlier exact-string MISSes were pypdf intra-word spacing artifacts ('us e', 'release ,'), resolved with a whitespace-insensitive match.

NASA Commercial Crew blog (2021-04-23) fetched via WebFetch. Stored excerpt 'First reuse of the Crew Dragon spacecraft and Falcon 9 rocket on a crew mission - Crew Dragon Endeavour flew the historic Demo-2 mission and the Falcon 9 flew astronauts on the Crew-1 mission' returned verbatim. No standalone numeric claim; the 'first reuse on a crew mission' qualitative fact is directly stated. Supports falcon9_reusable_launch_branch.

SpaceX EU Prospectus (BaFin-approved, 2026-06-05) PDF fetched (WebFetch returned binary; extracted locally with pypdf, 400pp). Stored excerpt 'Comprising the Super Heavy booster (powered by 33 Raptor engines) and the Starship upper stage (with three sea-level and three vacuum Raptor engines), Starship V3 is designed to deliver 100 metric tons to space in a fully reusable configuration' is verbatim. Numbers supported at the right basis: 33 Raptor engines (Super Heavy), 3 sea-level + 3 vacuum Raptor (Starship upper stage), 100 metric tons to space (Starship V3, fully reusable). Owner identity 'Space Exploration Technologies Corp.' also present, supporting org_spacex. Issuer evidence (not independent technical validation) - correctly labelled as such on the record.

FAA Starship/Super Heavy stakeholder page. WebFetch 403s (bot block, as record notes); fetched via curl with browser UA (HTTP 200, 113KB). Stored excerpt 'Under the Proposed Action, the FAA would modify SpaceX's existing vehicle operator license to authorize: Up to 25 annual Starship/Super Heavy orbital launches, including: Up to 25 annual landings of Starship (Second stage) Up to 25 annual landings of Super Heavy (First stage)' is verbatim. The 25-annual cadence figure is supported at the licensing/Proposed-Action basis. NOTAM / Aircraft Hazard Area / airspace language also present on the page, backing the range-safety sub-claim. (Record already carried owner reviewStatus 'reviewed'; this is an independent machine re-confirm - I do NOT emit reviewStatus.)

NASA Kennedy Orbiter TPS PDF (8pp) fetched (WebFetch returned binary; extracted locally with pypdf). All fragments verbatim: 'An average of 50 tiles are replaced after each mission, either due to handling damage or accumulated repairs.' (50-tile figure supported at per-mission basis); 'The tiles are bonded to the orbiter with a silicone adhesive.'; 'The tiles are first bonded to a strain isolator pad'; 'a light-weight, reusable thermal protection system composed of entirely new materials'. Note: this is Shuttle-orbiter TPS evidence used by analogy to back the Starship tile maintenance/bonding/inspection BOTTLENECK logic (not a SpaceX-specific tile spec); the record's summary frames it that way correctly.

repaired.excerpt: The first stage of the SpaceX Falcon 9 launch vehicle can land vertically, making it recoverable and therefore reusable. Many components contribute to the control system used for reentry and landing. One of these components is the grid fins. Located near the top of the rocket's first stage, grid fins are deployed during reentry. They help control lift during reentry, thereby guiding the booster to a soft landing on a landing pad or on a spaceport drone ship.
repaired.basis: Smithsonian NASM object record (Falcon 9 flown grid fin, Koreasat-5A, 2017-10-30); qualitative function/recovery description, no numeric claim
repaired.reason: Missing excerpt repaired with verbatim Smithsonian object text. FULLY supports falcon9_grid_fin_reentry_control (grid fins deployed during reentry, control lift during reentry, guide booster to soft landing). CAVEAT for the orchestrator: the record also lists falcon9_boostback_entry_landing_burns, but this page does NOT name the boostback / entry / landing BURN sequence (the propulsive maneuvers) - it only says the stage 'can land vertically', describes a 'soft landing', and a 'control system used for reentry and landing'. Recommend the orchestrator either (a) narrow this evidence's supportsNodeIds to falcon9_grid_fin_reentry_control only, or (b) treat its link to falcon9_boostback_entry_landing_burns as qualitative/landing-context only and source the burn-sequence claim separately. I did NOT fabricate a burns quote.
